column1: # The sentences over 30 words that docs/scripts/prose lets stay.
# Each entry is one line of three fields separated by tabs:
# PAGE is the page's path from the top of the checkout. SENTENCE is the
# sentence exactly as docs/scripts/prose prints it. REASON says why the
# sentence stays over 30 words, for example because it quotes a long string.

column2: The record says in a short phrase what the issue is about: what the work builds, what was found, or what was decided, as in "the work that draws right-to-left text".
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: It takes the place of getty, the program that normally displays the login prompt.", not "vtium runs on a Linux virtual terminal (VT), one of the text screens that Ctrl+Alt and a function key switch to, in place of getty, the program that prints the login prompt there."
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: Use the words readers already use for a thing, in pages people read: "renders", "images", "display server", "on supported hardware", not the project's own "draws", "pictures" or "where the machine has one".
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: Mention something it lacks only where a reader would expect it, and then in a sentence of its own: "It can render entirely on the CPU, so a GPU is optional.", not "It draws with no display server and no GPU."
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: Start an explanation from what the reader knows and move to what they don't, as VTium in depth starts from input and output on computers the reader has used before it reaches the VT.
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: For example, "A frit of bitmap sources that states no cell takes its fonts' own cell" becomes "A frit made only of bitmap fonts, with no `cell=` line, draws at the fonts' own glyph size."
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: A second example of unpacking: "Under the closed policy, a keyboard no rule mentions types nowhere, the guards are off, and no failure of vtium hands its VT to a getty's login prompt."

column2: Once a paragraph has said what vtium does, the next sentence can say "it", or make the thing itself the subject: "Each image is anchored to a line of text and scrolls with it."
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: Name the thing again too wherever "it" could mean two things: write "vtium passes the cluster to the font helper, which shapes the cluster.", not "vtium passes the cluster to the font helper, and it shapes it."
column3: A writing rule that quotes its example in full, moved word for word from the root AGENTS.md into docs/AGENTS.md.

column2: Applied to every sentence at once, they produce prose that is repetitive, overly literal and roundabout, where the effort to follow a style is louder than the person explaining the software.
